newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's LDP may keep Kubo as finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Japan's LDP may keep Kubo as finance minister.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo, a member of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), may keep his job even if the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) captures a majority of seats in Lower House elections on Sunday, financial market sources said on Friday.
"The LDP, seeking to keep its partnership with the Social Democratic Party, could move to retain Kubo in office," one financial market source said.
The SDP party, one of the LDP's coalition partners in the outgoing government, is widely expected to suffer a major setback in Sunday's poll.
Recent voter surveys have showed that Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's LDP party is likely to win a simple majority in the 500-seat Lower House of parliament.

However, the LDP does not have a majority in the Upper House and needs the Social Democratic Party's support to pass bills, other than those for the budget and treaties, in the Diet, financial sources said.
A former Finance Ministry official said that there is also a possibility that LDP Secretary-General Koichi Kato will replace Kubo as finance minister as a reward for his past service to the party.
